item.title: Is Nepal's flood a harbinger of what's to come in the Himalayas?
item.description: Building dams and hydropower plants in the Himalayas holds great promise for providing electricity. In the wake of the Nepal disaster, experts are asking about the risks of such construction.

item.title: Will FDA advisers recommend a multi-cancer blood test for approval? They'll vote
item.description: The company Grail says its Galleri blood test can detect up to 50 forms of cancer. An independent panel of experts will decide if the test should be recommended for FDA approval.
item.content:encoded: The company Grail says its Galleri blood test can detect up to 50 forms of cancer. An independent panel of experts will decide if the test should be recommended for FDA approval.

item.title: Trump administration drops 760,000 Americans from ACA coverage, citing fraud
item.description: Citing widespread fraud, JD Vance and Dr. Mehmet Oz announced 760,000 Americans had been kicked off health insurance purchased in the federal ACA marketplace. The move raises lots of questions.

item.title: Trump administration to remove 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees over fraud claims
item.description: White House officials allege these individuals were fraudulently enrolled in the program or do not exist. Vice President Vance said the move would save $2.2 billion.

item.title: Is produce from a home garden safer than store bought? 'It depends'
item.description: Home gardening is getting a boost, in part, from fears of foodborne illness. But is homegrown safer? Experts weigh in.

item.title: Abortion is on the ballot again as post-Roe policies continue to evolve
item.description: Four states will vote on abortion-related ballot measures in November. The measures follow the Supreme Court's "Dobbs" decision, which upended federal abortion protections.

item.title: Your smartwatch isn't accurately counting how many calories you burn, study says
item.description: A new study finds that consumer-grade fitness wearables are generally inaccurate when calculating calories burned. NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with the study's lead author Jason Kostrna.

item.title: Is produce from a home garden safer than store bought? 'It depends'
item.description: A record-breaking summer for foodborne illness prompted more consumers to grow produce at home. But experts say it's the farming practices, not size, that matters for food safety.

item.title: These stunning photos capture the hard yet fulfilling lives of fisherfolk
item.description: In the bustling heart of the southern Indian city of Chennai is a market that never sleeps, where residents from the poorest neighborhoods wage a battle of survival with the sea.

item.title: Betel nuts are a top mind-affecting substance. Now there's evidence of ancient use
item.description: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.
